See also: motoristă

Catalan

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From motor +‎ -ista.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): (Central) [mu.tuˈɾis.tə]
  • IPA(key): (Balearic) [mo.tuˈɾis.tə]
  • IPA(key): (Valencia) [mo.toˈɾis.ta]

Noun

[edit]

motorista m or f by sense (plural motoristes)

  1. motorist

Further reading

[edit]
  • “motorista”, in Diccionari de la llengua catalana [Dictionary of the Catalan Language] (in Catalan), second edition, Institute of Catalan Studies [Catalan: Institut d'Estudis Catalans], April 2007
  • “motorista”, in Gran Diccionari de la Llengua Catalana, Grup Enciclopèdia Catalana, 2026
  • “motorista” in Diccionari normatiu valencià, Acadèmia Valenciana de la Llengua.
  • “motorista” in Diccionari català-valencià-balear, Antoni Maria Alcover and Francesc de Borja Moll, 1962.

Cebuano

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From English motorist.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • Hyphenation: mo‧to‧ris‧ta

Noun

[edit]

motorista

  1. a motorist

Quotations

[edit]

For quotations using this term, see Citations:motorista.

Czech

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [ˈmotorɪsta]

Noun

[edit]

motorista m anim (female equivalent motoristka)

  1. motorist (one who drives a motor vehicle)

Declension

[edit]
Declension of motorista (masculine animate in -a)
singular plural
nominative motorista motoristé, motoristi
genitive motoristy motoristů
dative motoristovi motoristům
accusative motoristu motoristy
vocative motoristo motoristé, motoristi
locative motoristovi motoristech
instrumental motoristou motoristy

Related terms

[edit]
  • See motiv
  • motorismus

Further reading

[edit]
  • “motorista”, in Příruční slovník jazyka českého (in Czech), 1935–1957
  • “motorista”, in Slovník spisovného jazyka českého (in Czech), 1960–1971, 1989

Galician

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From motor +‎ -ista.

Noun

[edit]

motorista m or f by sense (plural motoristas)

  1. motorcyclist, biker

Italian

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From motore +‎ -ista.

Noun

[edit]

motorista m or f by sense (masculine plural motoristi, feminine plural motoriste)

  1. auto mechanic, motor mechanic

Further reading

[edit]
  • motorista in Treccani.it – Vocabolario Treccani on line, Istituto dell'Enciclopedia Italiana

Anagrams

[edit]
  • stortiamo

Portuguese

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From motor +‎ -ista.

Pronunciation

[edit]
 
  • (Brazil) IPA(key): /mo.toˈɾis.tɐ/
  • (Brazil) IPA(key): /mo.toˈɾis.tɐ/
    • (Rio de Janeiro) IPA(key): /mo.toˈɾiʃ.tɐ/
    • (Southern Brazil) IPA(key): /mo.toˈɾis.ta/
  • (Portugal) IPA(key): /mu.tuˈɾiʃ.tɐ/

  • Audio (Brazil (Caipira)):(file)
  • Rhymes: (Brazil) -istɐ, (Portugal, Rio de Janeiro) -iʃtɐ
  • Hyphenation: mo‧to‧ris‧ta

Noun

[edit]

motorista m or f by sense (plural motoristas)

  1. driver, motorist
    Ele é motorista de ônibus. ― He's a bus driver.
  2. chauffeur

Derived terms

[edit]
  • banco do motorista
  • carteira de motorista
  • motorista de fim de semana
  • motorista de praça

Descendants

[edit]
  • → Tetum: motorista

Further reading

[edit]
  • “motorista”, in Dicionário Aulete Digital (in Portuguese), Rio de Janeiro: Lexikon Editora Digital, 2008–2026
  • “motorista”, in Dicionário infopédia da Lingua Portuguesa (in Portuguese), Porto: Porto Editora, 2003–2026
  • “motorista”, in Michaelis Dicionário Brasileiro da Língua Portuguesa (in Portuguese), São Paulo: Editora Melhoramentos, 2015–2026, →ISBN
  • “motorista”, in Dicionário Priberam da Língua Portuguesa (in Portuguese), Lisbon: Priberam, 2008–2026

Romanian

[edit]

Noun

[edit]

motorista f

  1. definite nominative/accusative singular of motoristă

Spanish

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From motor +‎ -ista.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /motoˈɾista/ [mo.t̪oˈɾis.t̪a]
  • Rhymes: -ista
  • Syllabification: mo‧to‧ris‧ta

Noun

[edit]

motorista m or f by sense (plural motoristas)

  1. biker, motorcyclist
    Synonym: motociclista

Further reading

[edit]
  • “motorista”, in Diccionario de la lengua española [Dictionary of the Spanish Language] (in Spanish), online version 23.8.1, Royal Spanish Academy [Spanish: Real Academia Española], 15 December 2025

Tagalog

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from Spanish motorista. By surface analysis, motor +‎ -ista.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • (Standard Tagalog) IPA(key): /motoˈɾista/ [mo.t̪oˈɾis.t̪ɐ]
  • Rhymes: -ista
  • Syllabification: mo‧to‧ris‧ta

Noun

[edit]

motorista (Baybayin spelling ᜋᜓᜆᜓᜇᜒᜐ᜔ᜆ)

  1. motorcyclist; biker
    Synonym: motosiklista
  2. motorist (one who drives a motor vehicle)
    Synonyms: tagamaneho, drayber

See also

[edit]
  • drayber
